    Parabolic SAR

    Parabolic SAR is a level drawn as one dot below or above price, which closes in on price faster and faster as a trend runs on. Dots below price count as direction up, dots above as down; when price reaches the dot, the dots switch to the other side. The "parabolic" in its name comes from the curve the dots trace along a trend.

    Which question does Parabolic SAR answer?

    Parabolic SAR answers this question: while the trend runs, where is the trailing level and how close is price to it? One dot is drawn for each candle. In a rise the dots sit below the candles, in a fall above them.

    The dots do not close in at a constant speed. Each time the trend makes a new high or low, the acceleration factor grows and the dots approach price faster. So in a long trend the dots trace a curve; when the trend pauses, price reaches the dots quickly.

    How it is calculated

    1. Take the starting level and the extreme point. In a rise, SAR starts near the last low and the extreme point (EP) is the trend's highest value; in a fall it is the other way round.
    2. Move the level toward the extreme each candle. New SAR = previous SAR + acceleration factor (AF) × (EP − previous SAR). AF starts at 0.02 by default.
    3. Speed up as the trend extends. Each new high (in a rise) or new low (in a fall) raises AF by 0.02, up to 0.20. The larger the factor, the faster the dots close in.
    4. Switch sides when price reaches the dot. If the candle's wick reaches the SAR level, the direction turns; the new SAR starts at the previous trend's extreme point and AF resets to 0.02. SAR may not enter the range of the two previous candles.

    How it is commonly read

    • Dots below price: direction up; the level trails price from below.
    • Dots above price: direction down; the level trails price from above.
    • Dots speeding up: as the trend makes new extremes, the dots close in faster. Dots very close to price show that even a short pause may be enough to switch sides.
    • A switch of side: the dots moving to the other side describes that price reached the trailing level; it does not show that the new direction will last.

    The default setting is 0.02 start, 0.02 step and a 0.20 cap. A larger step makes the dots close in faster and switch sides more often.

    Same dots, different market

    Parabolic SAR behaves very differently depending on the structure of the market.

    Long trend

    The dots trace a clear curve on one side of price. As long as pullbacks do not reach the dots, the side does not change.

    Sideways market

    As price moves back and forth in a range, the dots switch sides often; each switch may be short-lived.

    A slowing trend

    Because the accelerated dots are very close to price, even a slowdown can cause a switch; that may describe a pause rather than a turn of the trend.

    What it shows, what it does not prove

    What it shows

    • The current direction and the level trailing price
    • That the trend speeds up as it makes new extremes
    • How close price is to the trailing level

    What it does not prove

    • That a switch of side is a lasting turn; in a sideways market it is often wrong
    • How long a trend will last
    • That a level is support or resistance; the dot is a calculated level

    The MarketLevelMap view

    How it relates to zones

    SAR dots are calculated from the trend's extreme point and its duration, not from areas where the market reacted before. So they should not be read like a support or resistance zone.

    Looking at them with zones still gives context. If the dots have sped up a lot as price approaches a resistance zone, even a short pause at the zone may be enough for the dots to switch sides. That says two separate observations happened at the same time, not that the zone held.

    Parabolic SAR in crypto

    Crypto prices can leave long wicks in a short time. Because SAR responds to wicks, a single long wick can make the dots switch sides even if the close stays on the old side. That is why switches are more frequent on lower timeframes.

    Often confused with

    • SupertrendBoth draw a level that trails price. Parabolic SAR speeds up as the trend runs on and turns on a wick; Supertrend measures the distance with ATR and turns on a close.
    • What is a trend?A trend is the structure of highs and lows; Parabolic SAR shows not that structure but a level that speeds up relative to the latest extreme.

    Key points

    • Parabolic SAR is a level drawn as dots that closes in on price faster as a trend runs on.
    • Dots below mean direction up; dots above mean direction down.
    • Default setting: 0.02 start, 0.02 step, 0.20 cap.
    • In sideways markets the dots switch sides often.
